audit_notes: Functional graph (out-degree 1 everywhere): count pairs (u,v) with v reachable from u. Each connected component is a rho-shape (tree-of-paths attached to a unique cycle). Honest solve: SCC / cycle decomposition + tree-DP over the cycle's trees. Unavoidable construct: worklist (cycle detection + reachability count).

Count strings length 1..K over 26 letters with per-letter usage caps C_i, modulo p. Canonical solve: 26-step DP where state f[k] = number-of-arrangements-of-multiset-of-length-k, transitioning by convolving with the i-th letter's polynomial (1 + x/1! + ... + x^{C_i}/C_i!). Non-local recurrence — each step's state depends on the full prior polynomial. Unavoidable construct: non-local DP recurrence over polynomial state.

Cascading water-flow over A_0..A_N with conditional left→right propagation; report first-time-positive operation count per i. Canonical solve: monotonic stack of (height, cumulative-cost) pairs, popping when next bar is taller. Sequential state with data-dependent control flow; the per-i answer cannot be computed independently. Unavoidable construct: sequential state evolution / monotonic stack maintenance.

Expected position of black ball after K Markov-chain swap operations on N positions, modulo p. With N up to ~10^9 and K up to 10^5, the canonical solve is a closed-form linear recurrence: p[k+1] = (1 - 2(N-1)/N^2) p[k] + 2(N-1)/N^3 — iterate K times. The K=10^5 iteration is sequential carried-state arithmetic; no fold can express the K-step recurrence without iteration. Unavoidable construct: K-step linear recurrence (or matrix exponentiation = log K matmuls — still requires iteration).

Minimum travel distance visiting all N tree-cities (start anywhere). Closed-form expression: 2·(sum of all edge weights) − (longest path between any two leaves) = 2·sum_edges − tree_diameter. Computing the diameter requires tree DP (two BFS/DFS passes). Unavoidable construct: tree DP / diameter via worklist.

Single-source shortest path (with vertex weights + edge weights) on a sparse undirected graph, N, M up to 2·10^5. Canonical solve: Dijkstra with priority queue. Worklist algorithm with data-dependent dequeue order; no fold over the adjacency lists expresses the relaxation correctly because relaxation order matters. Unavoidable construct: priority-queue worklist (Dijkstra).
